summary.signal: Aerospace AI is moving deeper into operational engineering loops: inspection and predictive MRO are producing measurable workflow metrics while engine production capacity is being redistributed under controlled qualification.

Engineering AI is becoming more executable and verifiable: quantum-assisted CAE, explicit CAD constraint checking and MCP-enabled MBSE connect AI to established engineering tools rather than stopping at text generation.

Scientific and engineering surrogates are retaining explicit high-fidelity anchors: hidden aerodynamic challenge sets, adaptive fidelity in turbine CFD and DFT confirmation in materials discovery constrain what the ML layer is allowed to claim.
Enterprise agent governance is consolidating around identity, MCP/tool governance, sandboxing, tracing and continuous evaluation outside the model itself.
Workforce evidence points to validation and exception handling as real AI workload: IBM's survey reports substantial invisible work and a gap between CHRO priorities and employee skill perceptions.

central_signals: Engineering AI value is increasingly determined by whether AI can execute inside established engineering workflows with traceable verification and override boundaries.
Aerospace adoption is expanding from design into inspection, MRO and production-system capacity, where quality and qualification constraints dominate.
Scientific AI is most credible when lower-cost ML screening or surrogates are explicitly anchored to hidden tests, high-fidelity CFD, DFT or physical evidence.
Agent governance is becoming infrastructure: identity, MCP/tool access, sandboxing, observability and evaluation are emerging as control-plane responsibilities.
Enterprise AI productivity claims should account for hidden human validation and exception-handling work rather than treating model output as zero-cost automation.
tensions_or_caveats: IonQ CAE acceleration, RTX MRO performance and several product capability metrics are first-party or vendor-reported and are not independent replication.
ONERA neural-field, CIT-CAD and turbomachinery MSFO results are author-reported preprint results and should retain that attribution.
IBM CHRO results are self-reported survey evidence, not causal proof of productivity or skill effects; the Scout excerpt's 60% statistic was corrected from executives to employees.
Oerlikon rare-earth-free coating details are supported by Reuters, but bounded verification did not locate a first-party technical release for the specific Mg/Ca zirconia formulation.
Exact published duplicates for SimScale Onshape, the GeoTransolver wind-tunnel surrogate and the ILO China enterprise-AI study were suppressed.

known_gaps: The specific Oerlikon rare-earth-free coating formulation is not backed by a located first-party technical note; it is preserved only as a wildcard based on Reuters reporting.
Honeywell vertical-integration and Aequs Hosur capacity signals are available primarily through secondary reporting, so they remain backlog rather than selected.
Quantum-accelerated CAE remains an early vendor-reported research result without independent replication in the bounded verification pass.
Several promising CAD/DFM papers are preprints, and full downstream manufacturability or production value is not yet established.

selected.practical_implication: Evaluate feature hierarchy, parameter/constraint correctness, Boolean and sketch semantics, and deterministic repair in addition to geometry overlap.

selected.practical_implication: Monitor where low-fidelity bias changes across design space and reserve high-fidelity evaluations for locally unreliable regions.
